data.hypothesis: Splitting the source-tile loop around the target index may remove per-pair self-index checks while preserving ordered accumulation and avoiding evaluation of a potentially overflowing self-force. This branch-avoidance adaptation is unmeasured; its variable loop bounds and helper calls may offset any benefit.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use this only as a measured candidate atop the valid shared-memory and inverse-cube base; keep that base if the split loops regress.
memory_lessons.claim: The current integrated base is valid at 0.0006500 s. A correct T3 program using a Newton-refined reciprocal and split source ranges measured 0.0012479 s, so the idea's benefit in the tiled kernel is uncertain.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare the full adapted kernel's correctness and timing with the current base; do not infer performance from the standalone trial.

data.notes: Only src/nbody_kernel.cu changed; src/launch.json remains at the base's 128-thread, 128-items-per-block, 4096-byte shared-memory configuration. This candidate needs fresh compilation, full correctness checks, and timing; no speedup is claimed.
transformations: Retained the measured shared-memory source tile, inverse-cube correction, and base launch settings.
Adapted split-range self-exclusion: for a tile containing the active target, process entries before and after it in order; process other tiles in one full range.
Factored the unchanged pair-force calculation into a force-inlined device helper to share it between the loop ranges.
